newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-STORM HALTS PLAY AT LOCH LOMOND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-STORM HALTS PLAY AT LOCH LOMOND.

text.p: Thunder, lightning and heavy rain forced a suspension of play midway during the second round of the Loch Lomond World Invitational on Thursday.
The storm sent the players scurrying for shelter with just under half the 153-man field having completed their rounds and with three groups still to tee off.
Reigning British Open champion Tom Lehman headed the scoreboard on 10 under par when he was forced off the course after 11 holes of his round.

He was one shot ahead of joint first-round leader Joakim Haeggman of Sweden, who had moved to nine under through 14 holes after sharing the first round lead with Paul Curry of England on 63, eight under par.
Steve Jones, the 1996 U.S. Open champion, was the leader in the clubhouse on eight under par after a second round 65. Curry was also eight under with two holes to complete.
